title: Phase 19.1 Attributed Graph Isomorphism & Literature Precedent Audit

scientific_originality_assessment.weisfeiler_lehman_screening: Candidate has distinct WL hash (e598cee54f0a95dd536dfc60ab1f15dc) differing from all 8 canonical grammar templates.
scientific_originality_assessment.attributed_isomorphism_result: Candidate is provably NOT isomorphic to any of the 8 canonical grammar families due to the introduction of an ungrounded floating intermediate shuttle connecting two serial flexure stages.
scientific_originality_assessment.literature_precedent_review: While structurally distinct from the 8 canonical grammar templates, the concept of multi-stage series intermediate shuttles is an established design motif in compliant mechanisms literature (e.g., Awtar & Slocum, 'Constraint-based design of parallel kinematic XY flexure mechanisms', ASME J. Mech. Des. 2007; Howell, 'Compliant Mechanisms', 2001). Therefore, Neodustria discovers this topology through autonomous compositional graph expansion rather than inventing a previously unknown physical concept in computational mechanics.
scientific_originality_assessment.formal_claim_boundary: The architecture is legitimately novel relative to Neodustria's predefined canonical template grammar, demonstrating generative compositional capability beyond fixed library selection. However, we refrain from claiming to have discovered a brand-new mechanical principle unknown to the global mechanical engineering community.
